text: Le match entre Kingsmoor FC et Westport Albion a tenu tout le monde en haleine avec un score final de 3-3. Viktor Quinlan a brillé en marquant 2 buts pour Kingsmoor, dont un penalty dès la 8e minute, un tir très attendu (xG 0.76, donc une belle chance en penalty) [#152]. Westport Albion a aussi fait preuve d’une attaque puissante avec plus de tirs et un total xG plus élevé (3.94 contre 3.4), ce qui veut dire qu’ils ont eu plus d'occasions nettes de marquer. Après des buts échangés en première période (2-2), chaque équipe a ajouté un but en seconde. Une expulsion à la 81e minute a compliqué les choses pour Kingsmoor, mais Luca Iversen a réussi un joli but qui a ravivé l’espoir [#1495][#1516]. Les deux équipes ont montré leur style unique : Kingsmoor jouait large avec des centres, tandis que Westport misait sur des passes rapides dans l’axe. Quel match captivant !

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Viktor Quinlan scored 2 goals including a penalty with a total xG of 1.44, contributing significantly to Kingsmoor FC's 3 goals [#152, #222].
- Westport Albion had a higher total xG of 3.94 compared to Kingsmoor FC's 3.4, reflecting more offensive threats overall [team_stats].
- The match ended in a 3-3 draw with both teams scoring 2 goals in the first half and 1 goal each in the second half [final_score, first_half, second_half].
- Felix Barros received a red card (second yellow) for Kingsmoor FC at 81' when the score was 2-3, impacting the team's chances late in the match [#1495].
- Kingsmoor FC made a tactical change at 65' to press higher and play more direct but failed to increase xG immediately afterwards [#1187].

- Kingsmoor FC’s first goal at 8' was a penalty scored by Viktor Quinlan after a foul led to the spot, demonstrating an early defensive lapse by Westport Albion under pressure [152]. This reflects Kingsmoor’s 4-4-2 setup with a wide, crossing style that likely led to an attacking overload situation forcing the penalty.
- The second Kingsmoor goal at 12' arose after a sustained build-up from a ball regain, involving 8 passes over 27 seconds and coordinated play mainly through midfield and wide areas, ending with the assisted finish by Quinlan from 8.8m [222]. This shows their wide crossing play and patient exploitation of spaces in Westport’s defensive structure via buildup from the back.
- Westport Albion responded with two goals at 22' and 30' from rapid, direct vertical passing moves starting from ball regains involving fewer but quicker passes and effective crossing delivery (e.g., assist by Dylan Rahman from a cross for the 30' goal) [401,553]. This aligns with their direct, vertical passing style in a 4-4-2 aiming to quickly exploit transition spaces.
- Kingsmoor’s equalizer at 82' came shortly after regaining possession through only 2 quick passes within 9 seconds, finished by Luca Iversen assisted by Mason Morales’s cross [1516]. This reflects a switch to a higher press and more direct play following the tactical change at 65', capitalizing on Westport’s deeper defensive block and reduced press following their tactical drop at 79' [1187,1459].
- Westport’s higher intensity pressing (lower PPDA at 5.5 vs Kingsmoor’s 7.8) and higher shot count (18 vs 10) show their emphasis on vertical passing and quick transitions, whereas Kingsmoor’s higher possession and crossing attempts (3 corners vs 5) underline their wide, patient build-ups in a 4-4-2 formation. Both teams adapted tactics mid-game reflecting their styles, influencing goal timings and ball recovery patterns.
